entityDescription: The ultimate goal of HOSTmi is the establishment of platform economics in the global space market, thereby improving the sustainable growth of the industry. The development of a dedicated online space market place adapted to the needs of the industry lays the foundation for standardized processes efficiently hooking up more payloads with flight opportunities. HOSTmi addresses the issue of bringing space payload owners and suitable space mission providers (providers of platform and service) together by creating a web-based automated online platform and by acting as an honest broker. By offering Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS), HOSTmi acts independently to best match space experiments and other payloads with the most suitable flight opportunities worldwide. PaaS means neutrally serving both the demand and supply side by facilitating a ‘matchmaking process’ between clients and suppliers. Clients - space experiment or payload owners - can use search criteria to define requirements in detail, as well as generate an in-situ ‘match’ with hosts and flight opportunities. These clients, for instance, can specify payload size, mass, power consumption and more technical details to search for possible hosting opportunities. HOSTmi, in turn, provides the secure infrastructure and centralized supplier services in contrast to the arguably highly fragmented offers in today’s market. Moreover, HOSTmi can provide access to mission-critical support services of third parties, such as centralized technical support, finance and insurance packages, as a digital one-stop-shop, thereby offering and bundling services over the lifecycle of a satellite. Given the NewSpace developments and multiple efforts towards modularity, building blocks and new standards, HOSTmi envisages an evolution of its service offering, including technology standards for experiment accommodation and interfaces with satellites and other space platforms

description:
Qt Group (Nasdaq Helsinki: QTCOM) is a global software company with a strong presence in more than 70 industries and is the leading independent technology behind millions of devices and applications. Qt is used by major global companies and developers worldwide, and the technology enables its customers to deliver exceptional user experiences and advance their digital transformation initiatives. Qt achieves this through its cross-platform software framework for the development of apps and devices, under both commercial and open source licenses.

Qt technology is used by approximately one million developers worldwide. We enable a single software code across all operating systems, platforms and screen types, from desktops and embedded systems to business-critical applications, in-vehicle systems, wearables and mobile devices connected to the Internet of Things.
In the space sector and more specifically for th development of downstream applications or services, our solution integrate efficiently with all the GIS and remote sensing environments (ArcGIS, Qgis, OTB, Google Earth,..). 
The company's net sales in year 2020 totaled 79.5 MEUR and it employs 348 people. The Qt Group operates in China, Finland, Germany, Japan, South Korea, Norway, Russia, the USA, France, UK, Italy and India.

Company description: The Institute for Systems and Robotics –ISR-Lisboa –is a multidisciplinary research institution in the areas of Robotics and Information Processing, including Systems and Control Theory, Signal Processing, Computer Vision, AI and Intelligent Systems and Biomedical Engineering.
Research at ISR-Lisboa spans a multitude of key topics, ranging from fundamental theoretical issues to the applications of engineering methods and tools to the design and analysis of complex systems. ISR-Lisboa is organized in the following 5 research groups/labs:Computer and Robot Vision;
- Dynamical Systems and Ocean Robotics;
- Evolutionary Systems and Biomedical Engineering;
- Intelligent Robots and Systems Group;
- Signal and Image Processing Group.
Across this broad spectrum our methodologies are rooted in solid mathematical principles, providing, whenever possible, formal guarantees of performance.
ISR-Lisboa is located at the North tower of the Lisbon campus of IST (Técnico – Lisboa) and is home to more than 100 researchers from many nationalities, including 32 faculty members, research fellows and Post-Doc researchers. They are responsible for the supervision of 65 post-graduate and 27 undergraduate students.
At ISR-Lisboa, we attach special attention to international scientific research cooperation and to advanced training and education initiatives through master, doctoral and post-doctoral programs. Grants are available for international students and researchers who wish to enroll in these programs.

description:
Indigo Legal is an advisory firm based in Brussels offering combined legal and regulatory expertise to high tech industry entities (including aerospace, aviation, information technology and satellite telecommunications) and governmental agencies. 
The independent firm is led by Mr. Patrick Michielsen, a senior legal advisor qualified under EU and Belgian law (i.e. often the chosen applicable laws for contracting under EU space projects), with more than 20 years of practitioner’s experience in all legal fields of technology law comprising general regulatory/legal advisory and contract drafting/negotiation work. Further to obtaining his specialist graduations in EU law, aviation & space law, Patrick has built up unique practical experience in the space industry with focus on satcom, earth observation and satnav (Galileo and Egnos). 
He served private tech industry clients and cooperated on various space technology study projects for ESA (i.a. Artes 10 and 20 feasibility studies) and for the EU Commission. He has also been instrumental in assisting numerous clients with their deployments in the area of satellite communications and other innovative technological applications. More broadly his experience also includes advisory work in the field of IT, telecommunications, intellectual property (IP), broadcasting law, transport law, geo data, data protection/security, R&D, funding, public procurement, and regulatory compliance for a wide range of clients. 
Prior to founding the independent law firm Indigo Legal, he worked for over more than a decade in the “top 1 tier” technology, media, telecommunications and aerospace departments of various major internationally oriented law firms in Brussels. He has been involved in technology dispute resolution and litigation matters. Furthermore he has worked on secondment in various multinational technology companies. 
Patrick has authored various legal articles on the aforementioned topics (e.g. UN Space Treaties and national space legislation) and he has acted as a legal speaker/trainer at various legal and industry events. He is also affiliated to various legal/technology associations, i.a. the European Centre of Space Lawyers (ESA) and Belgian engineering working groups in aerospace (including Cubesats). 
Indigo Legal offers its legal services in English, French and Dutch (working languages); combined with a sound practical knowledge of German, Italian and Spanish. 
Brussels Belgium T +32 489 922 839 E contact@indigolegal.eu

The private company ‘next level lab’ was founded in Duisburg, Germany, in May 2019 by David Kajkowski and Maximilian Schäfer. 
next level lab is a software development company focusing on business software and industry solutions.
The technology stack consists of web technologies (Angular, Ionic, JavaScript), various Microsoft .Net technologies in C# (server backend and frontend) and the creation of real-time 3D apps with Unity.
The tool stack is additionally extended by in-house design in 2D (Photoshop, Illustrator, Figma) and 3D (Blender, Substance Painter).
In the area of real-time 3D and Unity there is a strong focus on extended reality technologies: Augmented Reality with handheld devices, Mixed Reality with the Microsoft HoloLens (generation 1 & 2) and Virtual Reality in general.

These centers are specialized in the field of engineering sciences and not only, aiming at excellence in key multidisciplinary fields of society development, such as: information and communication technology; energy, environment and climate change; advanced production technologies and materials; safety and durability of constructions, etc. The aim is to interconnect these fields with doctoral, postdoctoral, and postgraduate training programs, as well as the transfer of know-how to society.
Most of the research activities carried out in UPT are financed by external sources obtained by participating in national and international calls, respectively by contracts with private companies. This represents a confirmation of the superior quality of the research and also of the prestige and professional deontology of the researchers affiliated to this institution. UPT has always been involved and still continues to be involved in a series of projects funded by national programs (funds provided by the Romanian Government through UEFISCDI, ANCSI), international programs (Horizon2020 Framework Program, European Cooperation in scientific and technical research, European Space Agency, Erasmus +, Bilateral Cooperation)..
UPT is currently developing fruitful collaboration with many universities in Europe, USA, Canada, South America and Asia, resulting in over 190 cooperation agreements concluded directly or under European Union programs.
